pf-investigate.description: Submit a repository_investigation run via Product Factory MCP
pf-investigate.template:
Use Product Factory MCP tools (not ad-hoc edits).

1. Call pf_submit with workflow=repository_investigation, repository_path set to the project root (or the path the user named), and request_text summarizing this investigation request (curated text only — do not dump the full chat):
$ARGUMENTS
2. Poll with pf_status / pf_tail until status is awaiting_approval or terminal.
3. Call pf_inspect and summarize the evidence report / artifacts for the user.
4. Do not approve unless the user explicitly asks.

pf-plan.description: Submit a technical_plan run via Product Factory MCP
pf-plan.template:
Use Product Factory MCP tools.

1. Call pf_submit with workflow=technical_plan, repository_path set appropriately, and curated request_text:
$ARGUMENTS
2. Poll pf_status / pf_tail until awaiting_approval or terminal.
3. pf_inspect and present the plan, acceptance criteria, and handoff tasks.
4. Do not approve unless the user explicitly asks.

pf-change.description: Submit a repository_change / code_change run via Product Factory MCP
pf-change.template:
Use Product Factory MCP tools for a durable change with budgets and approval.

1. Call pf_submit with workflow=repository_change (or code_change if more appropriate), repository_path set, optional validation_commands, and curated request_text:
$ARGUMENTS
2. Poll pf_status / pf_tail until awaiting_approval or terminal.
3. pf_inspect and summarize the plan, validations, and proposed patch.
4. Do not approve or apply unless the user explicitly asks — then use pf_approve (apply=false by default).

pf-status.description: Check Product Factory run status / recent events
pf-status.template:
Use Product Factory MCP.

If $ARGUMENTS looks like a run_id (run-…), call pf_status and pf_tail (after_seq=0 or the last cursor you have). Otherwise ask for the run_id or list what you know from this session.
Arguments: $ARGUMENTS

pf-approve.description: Approve a Product Factory run awaiting operator approval
pf-approve.template:
The user wants to approve a Product Factory run.

1. Interpret $ARGUMENTS as run_id (required). If missing, ask for it.
2. Call pf_inspect first and briefly confirm status is awaiting_approval.
3. Call pf_approve with apply=false unless the user explicitly asked to apply.
4. Report the HostResponse status.
Arguments: $ARGUMENTS
